lines.japanese: むかし、じいちゃんが言ってた。
lines.english: “Gramps once told us.”

lines.japanese: 消えるわけじゃない、みんなひとつになるんだ、って。
lines.english: “Nobody would disappear. We would all become one.”

lines.japanese: だから俺たちはその言葉を信じて踏みだしたんだ。
lines.english: “That was why we believed him, and took that step.”

lines.japanese: そりゃ恐くなかったわけじゃない。
lines.english: “Not that we weren't afraid.”

lines.japanese: ていうか恐かった。すげえ恐かった。
lines.english: “No, actually, we were. We were terrified.”

lines.japanese: そうだな……じゃあ、もしあんたが先の見えない毎日に疲れはててたとしよう。あとはみるみる老いてゆくだけだったとしようよ。
lines.english: All right... Say you were worn out by day after day with no end in sight. Say all you had left was to watch yourself getting older right before your eyes.

lines.japanese: そこで選択の機会が与えられるんだ。
lines.english: “Then somebody offers you a choice.”

lines.japanese: 『この冷凍カプセルに入って百年ぐらい寝ててごらん。目を覚ましたとき世界は変わってるよ。たぶんね。変わってなかったらごめん。あ、ちなみにこのカプセル、まだ臨床試験してないから』
lines.english: “Try climbing into this cryogenic capsule and sleeping for a hundred years or so. When you wake up, the world will have changed. Probably. Sorry if it hasn't. Oh, by the way, this capsule hasn't undergone clinical trials yet.”

lines.japanese: な、恐いだろ？
lines.english: “Scary, right?”

lines.japanese: だけど俺たちはみんな、もう他にすがるものがなかったから、じいちゃんの言葉と、目を覚ましたときに待っている未知の世界とを信じて、手を繋いだんだ。
lines.english: “But none of us had anything else left to cling to. So we trusted Gramps's words, trusted the unknown world waiting when we awoke, and joined hands.”

lines.japanese: ていう、まさしく実験みたいなものだった。
lines.english: “It really was an experiment.”

lines.japanese: 首尾よく成功したのかどうか、それはまだ分からない。
lines.english: “We still don't know whether it succeeded.”

lines.japanese: だけど俺たちは、いま、それぞれが一切の違和感も持たずここにいた。
lines.english: “But here we were now, every one of us, without the slightest sense that anything was wrong.”

lines.japanese: ひとつに重なって、繋がって、絡まって、溶けあっていた。
lines.english: “We overlapped, joined, tangled together, and melted into one another.”

lines.japanese: ごく自然に、当たり前に、まるで昔からそうだったみたいに、疑いようもなく俺たちは──
lines.english: “It felt perfectly natural, perfectly ordinary, as though we'd always been this way. Beyond any doubt, we had—”

lines.japanese: ──俺になっていた。
lines.english: “—become me.”

lines.japanese: 気分はやや良好。
lines.english: “My mood: fairly good.”

lines.japanese: 身体が疲れてるのか、ちょっと重苦しい濁りが混じってはいたけれど、どろんとしたまどろみの中に春の陽だまりが射してるカンジ。
lines.english: “Maybe my body was tired; there was a little heavy murk mixed in. Still, it felt like spring sunlight filtering into a thick, drowsy haze.”

lines.japanese: 一日中走りまわってくたくたの末に辿りついた、太陽の香りがする布団みたいな温かさ。
lines.english: “The warmth of bedding that smells of sunshine, reached at last after a whole day of running yourself ragged.”

lines.japanese: いまの俺たち──俺は、そんな気分だったんだ。
lines.english: “That was how we—how I—felt.”

lines.japanese: おっと、ごめんごめん。あんたへの挨拶を忘れてた。
lines.english: “Whoops. Sorry, sorry. I forgot to say hello.”

lines.japanese: よお、末っ子。初めまして久しぶり。元気か？　今日も観測ご苦労さま。
lines.english: “Hey, youngest brother. Pleased to meet you. Long time no see. How are you? Good work keeping watch today, as always.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは羽田鷹志。まあ、戸籍上はな。
lines.english: “We are Takashi Haneda. Legally, anyway.”

lines.japanese: 実際のところは羽田鷹志であり、千歳鷲介であり、成田隼人であり、伊丹伽楼羅でもあるんだ。
lines.english: “In truth, we are Takashi Haneda, Shusuke Chitose, Hayato Narita, and Karura Itami too.”

lines.japanese: だからあんたは、俺たちのことを一番しっくりくる名前で呼んでくれればいいぞ。分かるだろ、いまの俺たち──俺にとって、あんまり名前は重要じゃないんだ。
lines.english: “So call us whichever name feels most natural. You understand, don't you? To us—to me, as I am now—names don't matter very much.”

lines.japanese: トイレのことを便所と呼ぼうが化粧室と呼ぼうが、大した変わりはないっていう──
lines.english: “It's like whether you call the toilet the john or the powder room. Not much difference—”

lines.japanese: ん？　いや、けっこう変わるか？
lines.english: “Hm? No, I guess there is kind of a difference.”

lines.japanese: まあいいや。続けよう、引きつづき俺たちの話だ。
lines.english: “Ah, well. Let's go on. Back to our story.”

lines.japanese: 主役は俺たち。舞台はいろいろ。
lines.english: “We're the leads. The stage keeps changing.”

lines.japanese: 誰かが言ってたろ、チャンネル変えれば世界も変わるって。
lines.english: “Somebody said it, didn't they? Turn the channel, and the world changes too.”

lines.japanese: タカシの空は、厳しい寒さに慣れてしまったくすんだ白だった。
lines.english: “Takashi's sky was a tarnished white, accustomed to the bitter cold.”

lines.japanese: 隼人の空は、まばゆい輝きを覆いかくしてくれる群青だ。
lines.english: “Hayato's sky was a deep indigo that hid the blinding light.”

lines.japanese: そんなふうに空の色が心のチャンネルで設定できるのだとしたら、そうだとしたら、俺たちの空はラブとピースとハッピーに満ちた華々しい薔薇色だ。
lines.english: “And if the color of the sky really can be set by the channel of the heart—if that's true—then our sky is a magnificent rose pink, overflowing with love and peace and happiness.”

lines.japanese: いや、勢いで言ってみたものの想像してみるとキモいな、薔薇色の空……。
lines.english: “No, I only said that because I got carried away. Now that I picture it, a rose-pink sky is pretty gross...”

lines.japanese: うん、じゃあ普通に、ドッピカーンな快晴だ。
lines.english: “Okay, then—just a dazzling, cloudless day.”

lines.japanese: 青い空！　白い雲！　燃えさかる太陽！
lines.english: “Blue sky! White clouds! A blazing sun!”

lines.japanese: っていうのはまあ、季節柄ちょっと難しいんだけど、そんなイメージで行ってみよう。
lines.english: “Which is a little difficult given the season, but let's go with that image.”

lines.japanese: これは俺たちの物語。
lines.english: “This is our story.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちに翼はないこともないんじゃないかなあ、っていう物語だぞ。
lines.english: “The story of how maybe—just maybe—it isn't quite true that we have no wings.”
